title: The Jerusalem Talmud
hookLine: sages in Galilee complete a Talmud, the teaching of the land itself

cards: One star in the sky: it's still day. Two stars: nobody's sure. Three stars: now it's night.
That rule of thumb comes from a conversation about yesterday's question, when the evening Shema may begin. The Mishnah said the time starts when the priests go in to eat their holy portion.
But what if you're standing outside, with no priest in sight? You look up and count. The sages who counted the stars lived in the land of Israel itself, in towns around the Galilee.
What they built is known by a name that points somewhere else entirely.

teach.h: MISHNAH PLUS GEMARA IS A TALMUD.
teach.b: Once the Mishnah was written, students did what students do: they asked questions of it. Why does this teacher say midnight? What's the source in the Torah?
What if the case is a little different? Their long, recorded discussion of the Mishnah is called Gemara, and Mishnah plus Gemara together is a Talmud. There are two.
Today's is usually called the Jerusalem Talmud, in Hebrew the Yerushalmi.

teach.h: NAMED FOR JERUSALEM, MADE IN GALILEE.
teach.b: But its sages taught in the Galilee, not in Jerusalem.

teach.h: THE TALMUD OF THE LAND OF ISRAEL.
teach.b: Its older names say where it came from: the Talmud of the Land of Israel, the Talmud of the West. You can feel the land in it.
It has Gemara on the order of Seeds, the farming laws: tithes, the corner of the field left for the poor, the seventh year when the land rests.
Laws tied to the soil of the land, discussed by sages who lived on it, in a language close to the Aramaic spoken around them. Some readers notice something else. The Yerushalmi can be terse.
Arguments start and stop; a question is raised and the page moves on. Some readers sense a work that was never fully smoothed out.
Students still learn it, unfinished edges and all, reading closely what is there.

how: The Jerusalem Talmud is studied in yeshivas and by individuals alongside the Babylonian Talmud, and is turned to especially for the farming laws of the land of Israel.

s: the Jerusalem Talmud was made in Jerusalem
its sages taught in the Galilee. older names call it the Talmud of the Land of Israel.
a Talmud is Mishnah plus Gemara
Gemara is the recorded discussion of the Mishnah.
the Yerushalmi skips the farming laws

games.q: you're a student outside at dusk, trying to know whether it's night yet. you see two stars. what do you say?
games.why: one star is day, three are night, and two leave it in doubt. the sages turned an abstract rule into something you can see.

practice: Bring to mind something left incomplete: a project you set down, a letter never sent, maybe something someone you love began and didn't finish.
Don't fix it or judge it; look at it the way students read the Yerushalmi, as worth learning from exactly as it is, and ask what the unfinished part tells you that a polished version wouldn't.
If you pray, you can give thanks for work that was begun.

wordCard.voice: Yerushalmi. The Jewish sages' name for what's usually called the Jerusalem Talmud, though its sages taught in the Galilee, not Jerusalem itself.
